obtained.how: secondary only: FishBase's egg-development and larvae pages for Esox niger (fishbase.se; fishbase.net.br refused with 403) and the Smithsonian NEMESIS species summary for golden shiner, which cite this atlas. The atlas itself (Volume I) has no open copy found: the Internet Archive scan is lending-only, HathiTrust and the NOAA repository refuse scripts with a bot check / 403, and the USGS Publications Warehouse record has no digital copy

bibliography.checked_against: the USGS Publications Warehouse record (fwsobs78_12), FishBase's reference 4639 and the NEMESIS reference list — not the title page
bibliography.note: title 'Development of fishes of the Mid-Atlantic Bight: an atlas of egg, larval, and juvenile stages', U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, FWS/OBS-78/12, 1978 (USGS); Volume I 'Acipenseridae through Ictaluridae' by P. W. Jones, F. D. Martin and J. D. Hardy Jr. (FishBase, NEMESIS). Page count (366 pp.) not checked; some catalogues list the three as editors

claims.claim: 11 d at 10.0 °C, 5 d at 14.4 °C, 2.5 d at 17.2 °C (Jones, Martin & Hardy 1978, via FishBase)
claims.note: FishBase lists exactly these three rows (locality 'Mid-Atlantic Bight') with Main Ref. 4639 = Jones et al. 1978, but its per-row data references differ: 2.5 d (range 2–3 d) at 17.20 °C → Underhill 1948 (ref. 39106); 5.00 d at 14.40 °C (range 12.2–16.6 °C) → Jones et al. 1978 (ref. 4639); 11.00 d at 10.00 °C → Miller 1962 (ref. 39118). So the atlas compiles them from Underhill and Miller; FishBase's 'Underhill 1948' may be a different item from the paper's Underhill 1949 (J. Wildl. Manage. 13: 377–391) — neither was read. Saved: Jones_etal_1978.fishbase_eggdev.html and _214/_215/_216.html

claims.claim: hatch length mode 7.2 mm 'in another series'
claims.note: FishBase's larvae page (Main Ref. Jones et al. 1978) gives yolk-sac larvae 'Length at birth' 5–7.9 mm, mode 7.2 mm (ref. 4639), Mid-Atlantic Bight; yolk-sac stage 6–8 days (Jones_etal_1978.fishbase_larvae.html)

claims.paper: src/species.js:265 (golden shiner Lmat 6.5, LmatM 6, matureAge 1.5 yr)
claims.claim: golden shiner matures at 5–7 cm, most in the second year (Jones et al. 1978)
claims.note: the NEMESIS summary (secondary) says golden shiners 'take between seven months and three years to mature, but most reach maturity in the second year at 50-70 mm (Jones et al. 1978)', and lists spawning at 20–27 °C from the same source; length type (TL/SL) not given there (Jones_etal_1978.nemesis_golden_shiner.html)
